scenarioName: Anxiety-Related Hyperventilation — Ruling Out Organic Causes

scenarioStory.history: Patient was at work when she suddenly began breathing rapidly, reports feeling like she 'can't get enough air' and numbness/tingling around her mouth and in her fingertips. Coworkers called 911 after she became visibly distressed. No known trigger identified other than a stressful phone call moments before onset.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 22-year-old female seated and breathing rapidly, reporting she can't catch her breath, with tingling around her mouth and in her fingers. She is anxious but alert and able to speak in full sentences. → Full assessment and reassurance provided: Crew completes a full assessment to rule out organic causes of the rapid breathing, confirms clear breath sounds and normal oxygenation, and provides verbal reassurance and coaching to help the patient slow her breathing. → Breathing slows, symptoms resolve: With reassurance and coaching, the patient's respiratory rate and heart rate normalize, tingling resolves, and she is transported for further evaluation in a position of comfort.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Rapid breathing and feeling like she can't catch her breath

scenarioEvents.name: Full assessment and reassurance provided
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes a full assessment to rule out organic causes of the rapid breathing, confirms clear breath sounds and normal oxygenation, and provides verbal reassurance and coaching to help the patient slow her breathing.
relatedChecklist: Obtain full vital signs, SpO2, and waveform capnography to rule out hypoxia or true respiratory pathology
Auscultate breath sounds and assess air entry; confirm clear, symmetric, no wheeze
Obtain focused history: onset, triggers, and concurrent symptoms to identify a psychogenic cause
Provide verbal reassurance and coached breathing; place patient in position of comfort

scenarioEvents.name: Breathing slows, symptoms resolve
scenarioEvents.description: With reassurance and coaching, the patient's respiratory rate and heart rate normalize, tingling resolves, and she is transported for further evaluation in a position of comfort.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and transport in position of comfort

scenarioEvents.name: Anxiety assumed without full assessment
scenarioEvents.description: The crew labels the episode as anxiety without auscultating breath sounds or trending SpO2/capnography. An evolving mild bronchospasm goes unrecognized as oxygenation begins to decline.
relatedChecklist: Recognize incomplete assessment; auscultate breath sounds and reassess SpO2 for true hypoxia/wheeze
